topic: Night-driving glare: why headlights dazzle and what helps

youtube.title: Headlights blinding you at night? 3 signs 🚗 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Do oncoming headlights blind you at night? Watch for these 3 signs.
இரவில் எதிர் விளக்கு கண்ணைக் கூசுகிறதா? இந்த 3 அறிகுறிகளைக் கவனியுங்கள்.

• In the dark your pupil opens wide, so any haze in the eye or smudge on your glasses scatters light into glare.
• Sign 1: halos or starbursts around streetlights and headlights.
• Sign 2: your sight takes longer to clear after a bright light passes.
• Sign 3: it gets worse every year - night glare is a common early sign of cataract.
• Clean the windscreen inside and out, keep glasses spotless, and look at the left edge of the road, not into the lights.
• Yellow 'night driving' glasses don't help; lenses with anti-reflective coating cut reflections.
• Sudden blur or loss of vision? See an eye specialist the same day.

topic: Single vision vs bifocal vs progressive: which do you need?

youtube.title: Single vision, bifocal or progressive? Which one? 👓 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Single vision, bifocal or progressive: which glasses do you actually need?
உங்களுக்கு எந்தக் கண்ணாடி சரி? எளிய விளக்கம்.

• After about 40, the lens inside the eye gets stiffer, so close-up focus gets harder (presbyopia).
• Single vision: one power across the lens - best when you need help for one distance only.
• Bifocal: two zones with a visible line - distance on top, reading below; the middle distance is missing.
• Progressive: no line - far, middle (computer, phone) and near flow smoothly in one lens.
• It can take a week or two to get used to progressives: wear them all day and turn your head, not just your eyes.

topic: Sunlight & UV: why your eyes need sunglasses in Chennai

youtube.title: Is Chennai sun hurting your eyes? ☀️😎 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Chennai sun is strong all year, and its UV light can harm your eyes, not just your skin.
சென்னை வெயில் கண்ணையும் பாதிக்குமா? இதோ எளிய பாதுகாப்பு.

• UV rays are invisible; they reach the eye's surface and the lens inside it, and the effect adds up over years.
• Studies show long-term sun exposure raises the risk of cataract and of fleshy growths on the white of the eye.
• Choose sunglasses marked 'UV400' or '100% UV protection' - a darker lens is not always safer.
• Add a cap or wide hat and use shade around midday.
• Protect children too: their eyes let in more UV, and sand and water reflect extra light.
• Never look straight at the sun, even during an eclipse. A sudden blind spot or blur needs an eye specialist urgently.

• Up close, a tiny focusing muscle in your eye works nonstop, and you blink less, so eyes dry out.
• Eye strain doesn't permanently damage your eyes, but even a small uncorrected power can make headaches worse.
• 20-20-20: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
• Keep the screen an arm's length away, slightly below eye level, with no window glare.
• Blink fully and often; read in good light.
• Urgent: a sudden severe headache with eye pain, redness, blurred vision or rainbow halos needs an eye specialist the same day.

topic: Blinking: we blink less on screens; simple blink exercise

youtube.title: When did you last blink? Try this 👁️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
When did you last blink? On screens, probably not for a while.
கடைசியாக எப்போது கண் சிமிட்டினீர்கள்? இந்தப் பயிற்சியை முயற்சியுங்கள்.

• Each blink spreads a fresh layer of tears that keeps the eye's surface smooth, clear and comfortable.
• Studies show we blink much less while staring at screens, and many blinks only close half way.
• Blink exercise: close gently, pause 2 seconds, squeeze softly, open. Repeat 10 times, a few times a day.
• Every 20 minutes, look far away; a cool, clean cloth over closed eyes can feel soothing.
• Don't rub your eyes, don't let a fan or AC blow straight on your face, and don't use random eye drops without advice.
• Urgent: eye pain, redness, light sensitivity or blur that doesn't clear when you blink needs an eye specialist.

topic: Colour vision deficiency: more common in men; simple facts

• The retina has three types of colour-sensing cells (cones) for red, green and blue.
• If one type works differently, some colours look alike.
• Studies show about 1 in 12 men, but only about 1 in 200 women, have colour vision deficiency.
• The common type passes down on the X chromosome; men have only one X.
• It's usually present from birth, doesn't get worse and is not blindness.
• A quick colour plate test during an eye test can find it: useful for school and some jobs.
• Colours suddenly looking faded, especially in one eye: see an eye specialist quickly.

• Eyelid twitching (myokymia) is a small eyelid muscle firing again and again; it usually settles by itself.
• Common triggers: poor sleep, stress, too much tea/coffee, long screen time, dry or tired eyes.

• See a doctor if it lasts more than a few weeks, the eyelid closes fully, the eye is red/swollen, or other face muscles twitch.
• General education only, not a diagnosis.

topic: Stye: warm compress, don't squeeze, see a doctor if it spreads

youtube.title: Stye on your eyelid? Don't squeeze it! 🚫 #Shorts
youtube.description:

இமையில் கட்டி? அழுத்தி பிழியாதீர்கள்!

• A stye is a blocked, infected oil gland near the lash line.
• Do: clean warm compress on the closed eye, about 10 minutes, 3–4 times a day.
• Do: wash hands before touching your eyes; keep the eyelid gently clean.
• Don't: squeeze or pop it, as it can push the infection deeper and spread it.
• Don't: wear eye makeup or contact lenses until it heals; replace old eye makeup.
• See a doctor if swelling spreads to the eyelid or cheek, the eye swells shut, vision changes, or it isn't better in about a week.
• Most styes settle in about a week. General education only.

topic: Smoking and eyes: raises cataract and AMD risk

youtube.title: Smoking hurts your eyes too: 3 facts 🚭 #Shorts

Smoking doesn't just hurt your lungs. 3 eye facts every smoker should know.
புகைபிடித்தல் கண்களையும் பாதிக்கும்.

• Smoke irritates and dries the surface of the eye, even for people nearby.
• Studies show smokers are more likely to get cataracts (the eye's clear lens turning cloudy).
• Smoking raises the risk of age-related macular degeneration (AMD), which damages central vision used for reading and faces.
• Why: smoke harms tiny blood vessels and puts extra stress on delicate eye tissue.
• Good news: quitting lowers your risk at any age. Walk daily, eat leafy greens and colourful vegetables.
• Keep BP and sugar in check; get a yearly eye test after 40.
• See an eye specialist soon if straight lines look wavy or a dark spot appears in the centre of your vision.

• In young children, not wearing needed glasses can affect how vision develops.
• Get children's eyes checked every year, adults regularly as your eye doctor advises.

• The macula is the centre of the retina; it gives sharp central vision for reading and faces.
• Sign 1: straight lines (door frames, tiles, text) look bent or wavy.
• Sign 2: a blurry or dark spot in the centre of vision. Sign 3: faces and small print get harder to see.
• Amsler grid check: hold a square grid at reading distance, wear your reading glasses, cover one eye, look at the centre dot. Note any wavy, blurred or missing lines. Repeat with the other eye.
• Studies show AMD is a leading cause of vision loss in older adults; smoking raises the risk.
• See an eye specialist urgently if lines suddenly turn wavy or a new dark spot appears.

• In thyroid eye disease, the immune system causes swelling in the muscles and tissue behind the eye.
• Sign 1: dry, gritty, red or watery eyes that don't settle.
• Sign 2: eyes look bigger or bulging, or the upper lid pulls back (a 'staring' look).
• Sign 3: double vision, or pain when moving the eyes.
• It's more common in women; smoking makes it worse. It can occur even when thyroid levels are under control.
• Don't smoke, wear sunglasses outdoors, and tell your doctor about any eye changes.
• See an eye specialist urgently if vision drops, colours look faded, or double vision starts suddenly.

youtube.title: Party popper at a face? One pop can hurt an eye 🎉 #Shorts

• The front of the eye (cornea) is thin and delicate, so fast paper, plastic or a cork can scratch or bruise it.
• Point party poppers up and away from everyone, never at faces.
• Open bottles pointing away from people, with a towel over the cork.
• Kids and crackers: arm's length, safety glasses, a bucket of water, and an adult beside them.
• If something hits the eye, don't rub, press or try to pull out anything stuck. Cover it gently and go to an eye hospital.
• See an eye specialist urgently for pain, bleeding, blurred vision or any burn.

topic: AC rooms and dry eyes: humidity, blinking, water, airflow away from face

youtube.title: AC all day and eyes burning? Here's why ❄️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
AC all day and your eyes burn by evening? Here's why. ❄️
AC அறையில் கண் எரிச்சலா? காரணம் இதுதான்.

• AC pulls moisture from the air, so your tear layer dries faster and eyes feel gritty or tired.
• We blink much less when we stare at a screen, which adds to the dryness.
• Turn the AC vent and fan away from your face, and don't set the AC too cold.
• Follow 20-20-20: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds and blink fully.
• Drink enough water; a bowl of water or plants nearby can help the air.
• See an eye specialist if redness, pain or blurred vision doesn't go away.

topic: Eyelid hygiene: crusty lashes, warm compress, gentle lid cleaning

காலையில் இமையில் பொடுகு போல் படிகிறதா?

• Tiny oil glands line your eyelids. When they block, oil and flakes build up at the lash line (often called blepharitis).
• Eyelid inflammation is very common, and simple daily care keeps it in check.
• Warm compress: a clean cloth with warm (not hot) water on closed eyes for 5–10 minutes.
• Then gently wipe along the lash line with a clean, damp cotton pad. Always wash your hands first.
• Don't rub, pick the crusts, or sleep in eye makeup.
• See an eye specialist for pain, swelling, a lump, or blurred vision.

topic: Teen's power keeps changing? Keratoconus signs

youtube.title: Teen's power keeps changing? It may be more than growing 👁️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
Your teen's power keeps changing? It may be more than growing up. 👁️
டீன் வயதில் கண்ணாடி பவர் அடிக்கடி மாறுகிறதா?

• The cornea is the eye's clear front window. In keratoconus it thins and bulges into a cone shape.
• Sign 1: power, especially cylinder, changes often.
• Sign 2: blurred, stretched or double vision, even with new glasses.
• Sign 3: glare and halos around lights, plus a strong eye-rubbing habit.
• It often starts in the teens. Found early, treatment can help slow it.
• Stop eye rubbing, get itchy allergies treated, and see an eye specialist for a cornea scan.

topic: Do kids need sunglasses? UV and young eyes

youtube.title: Do kids really need sunglasses? ☀️😎 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Sunglasses for kids: just style, or real protection?
குழந்தைகளுக்கு கூலிங் கிளாஸ் வெறும் ஸ்டைலா? உண்மை என்ன?

• A child's eye lens is clearer than an adult's, so more UV light reaches the back of the eye.
• UV damage adds up over a lifetime and is linked to cataract later in life.
• Clouds don't block UV. Sand, water and white walls reflect it back into the eyes.
• Choose sunglasses labelled UV400 / 100% UV protection, with a wide-brimmed hat.
• Avoid dark toy sunglasses without a UV filter: they make the pupil open wider.
• Plan outdoor play in shade between 10 am and 4 pm.
• School holidays are a good time for your child's yearly eye test.

topic: What does 6/6 vision mean?

youtube.title: 6/6 means perfect eyes? Quick quiz 👁️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
Does 6/6 mean perfect eyes? Quick quiz! 👁️
6/6 என்றால் என்ன அர்த்தம்?

• 6/6 means you read at 6 metres what a normal eye reads at 6 metres: normal sharpness, not 'perfect eyes'.
• 6/12 means you need to be at 6 m to read what others read from 12 m.
• The letter chart doesn't check eye pressure, side vision, the retina or near vision.
• Glaucoma can steal side vision while you still read 6/6.
• A full eye test checks all of these.
• Know your number: book a full eye test.

ஒரு கண் மட்டும் பலவீனமா?

topic: Droopy eyelid (ptosis) in elders and kids — get it checked

youtube.title: One eyelid drooping? 3 signs not to ignore 👁️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
Is one eyelid drooping? 3 signs you shouldn't ignore. 👁️
இமை கீழே தொங்குகிறதா?

• A small muscle lifts your eyelid; with age it can stretch and weaken (ptosis).
• Sign 1: tilting the chin up or raising the eyebrows to see.
• Sign 2: the lid covers part of the pupil, so the top of your view looks cut off.
• Sign 3: one eye looks smaller, often more noticeable by evening or in photos.
• In children, a droopy lid can block vision and lead to a lazy eye if not checked.
• Urgent: a lid that droops suddenly with double vision, severe headache or a weak face needs a hospital straight away. Most droopy eyelids can be treated.

topic: Kitchen eye safety: oil splash, chilli on hands, onion tears, smoke

youtube.title: Chilli in your eye? Kitchen eye safety 🌶️ #Shorts
youtube.description:
Chilli in your eye? Kitchen eye safety: do's and don'ts. 🌶️
மிளகாய் கண்ணில் பட்டதா? என்ன செய்வது?

• Chilli and onion release chemicals that trigger pain nerves on the eye's surface.
• Wash hands with soap and water after cutting chillies, before touching your eyes.
• If it gets in: keep the eye open under clean running water for several minutes.
• Don't rub, and don't put ghee, milk or any home remedy in the eye.
• Chilled onions and a sharp knife mean fewer tears. Stand back from hot oil.
• See an eye specialist urgently for pain, redness or blurred vision after rinsing, or any hot-oil burn.

காலையில் கண் வீக்கமா?

• Don't rub: it makes swelling and itching worse.
• Urgent: pain, redness, fever, a change in vision, or one eye badly swollen. If your feet swell too, see a doctor.

topic: Your tears have 3 layers: how tears protect your eyes

youtube.title: Your tears have 3 layers! Here's how they protect you 💧 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Did you know your tears have 3 layers? 💧
கண்ணீருக்கு 3 அடுக்குகள் உள்ளன!

• Oil layer (top): from tiny glands on the lid edges; stops tears drying too fast.
• Water layer (middle): from the tear glands; washes away dust and germs.
• Mucus layer (bottom): helps tears spread and stick evenly on the eye.
• Every blink spreads them, and studies show we blink less when staring at screens.
• Protect your tears: blink fully, take 20-20-20 breaks, keep AC and fan air off your face, and drink water.
• Painful red eye or sudden blur needs an eye specialist urgently. For ongoing dryness, book an eye test.

topic: Diabetes & your eyes: complete guide (why sugar affects the retina, symptoms, yearly dilated exam, tips)

youtube.title: Diabetes & your eyes: a complete, simple guide | LenzKare
youtube.description:
Diabetes and your eyes: everything you need to know, explained simply. 👁️
சர்க்கரை நோயும் உங்கள் கண்களும்: முழுமையான எளிய விளக்கம்.

• The retina at the back of the eye is fed by very fine blood vessels; years of high sugar can weaken them so they leak or get blocked (diabetic retinopathy).
• NEI: it is the most common cause of vision loss in people with diabetes.
• Early stages often have no pain and vision can seem normal, which is why a yearly dilated eye exam matters.
• Warning signs: blurry or changing vision, dark spots or floating specks, poor night vision, faded colours.
• Diabetes can also change your glasses power, bring cataract earlier and raise glaucoma risk.
• Keep sugar, BP and cholesterol in control as your doctor advises, walk daily, and don't smoke.
• Sudden loss of vision or a curtain over your sight: see an eye specialist the same day.

topic: Glaucoma: the silent thief of sight — complete explainer

youtube.title: Glaucoma: the silent thief of sight, fully explained | LenzKare
youtube.description:
Glaucoma: the silent thief of sight, explained simply. 👁️
கிளாக்கோமா: சத்தமில்லாமல் பார்வையைத் திருடும் நோய்.

• The optic nerve is the cable that carries pictures from the eye to the brain; glaucoma damages it, often with raised eye pressure.
• Side vision fades first while central vision stays clear, so most people don't notice; NEI says about half of people with glaucoma don't know they have it.
• Open-angle glaucoma is the most common: slow, painless, no early signs.
• Angle-closure can be sudden: severe eye pain, red eye, headache, haloes, nausea. That is an emergency: go to an eye hospital immediately.
• Higher risk: family history, age over 40, diabetes, high minus or plus power, long-term steroid use.
• Lost vision cannot be restored, but early treatment helps protect what you have; never stop prescribed treatment on your own.
• Get eye pressure, optic nerve and side-vision checks regularly, especially after 40.

• Digital eye strain: tired eyes, burning, blur, headache, plus neck and shoulder pain.

• Uncorrected power makes strain worse, so get an eye test and use the right glasses for screen distance.
• Painful red eye, light sensitivity or sudden blur: see an eye specialist urgently.

topic: How to read your prescription and choose the right lenses (single, bifocal, progressive, coatings, PD)

youtube.title: How to read your prescription & choose lenses | LenzKare
youtube.description:
How to read your glasses prescription and choose the right lenses. 👓
கண்ணாடி மருந்துச்சீட்டை எப்படி படிப்பது? சரியான லென்ஸ் எது?

• RE/OD = right eye, LE/OS = left eye.
• SPH is the main power: minus (−) means far is blurry, plus (+) means near is harder.
• CYL corrects astigmatism; AXIS (1–180) shows its direction, not its strength. ADD is extra plus power for reading, usually from the 40s.
• PD (pupillary distance) places each lens centre in front of your pupil; it must be measured correctly.
• Lens types: single vision (one distance), bifocal (far + near with a line), progressive (far, middle and near with no line).
• Options: anti-glare coating, photochromic (+₹1,000 on Fusion lenses), and thinner index for higher power (Fusion 1.50, 1.56, 1.60).
